Faithful wife of Odysseus, this legendary Queen of Ithaca famously used weaving schemes to stall over a hundred suitors — who is she?
Penelope: Wife of Odysseus in Greek mythology.
Born in the late 19th century and often hurled as an insult, this contested political stance pits the so-called 'common people' against a perceived elite — what is it?
Populism: Political ideology emphasising the "common people"
A war correspondent in Afghanistan and Angola in the 1980s, this Oxford-educated Polish statesman later became his country's Foreign Minister and, since 2025, also Deputy Prime Minister — who is he?
Radosław Sikorski: Polish politician and journalist (born 1963)

This political ideology holds that sovereignty belongs to the people and their elected representatives rather than a hereditary monarch, and champions civic virtue, anti-corruption, and freedom from domination — which ideology?
Republicanism: Political ideology centered on citizenship in a state organized as a republic.
Born in Hong Kong and educated at Eton, this British former diplomat and MP walked solo across Asia after leaving the Foreign Office, and now co-hosts a podcast with Alastair Campbell — who is he?
Rory Stewart: British politician, academic and broadcaster (born 1973)
Venerated as a prophet across three major faiths, this biblical figure guided Israel's transition from the age of judges to kingship, first anointing Saul and later David — who is he?
Born to a poor Cossack family and later a close ally of Stalin, this Soviet cavalry commander founded the Red Cavalry and became the subject of patriotic songs — who is he?
Only the second person to complete a full five-year term as Chief Minister of Karnataka, this Congress politician also served two stints as the state's Deputy Chief Minister — who is he?
Siddaramaiah: Chief Minister of Karnataka from 2013 to 2018 and 2023 to 2026.

Defined by a one-man police state, forced agricultural collectivization, and a sweeping cult of personality, this set of Soviet policies held sway from 1927 until the dictator's death in 1953 — what is it called?
Stalinism: Political and economic policies implemented by Joseph Stalin.
A military engineer who is a national hero in Poland, Lithuania, Belarus AND the United States, he fought for the American Revolution before leading an uprising in 1794 — who was he?
This centrist political position blends economically liberal ideas with social democratic policy, favoring workfare over welfare — what's it called?
Third Way: Centrist political position. The Third Way has been promoted by social liberal and social-democratic parties.
A law professor with a doctorate from the London School of Economics, she became the first woman to serve as president of the Republic of China, from 2016 to 2024 — who is she?

Tsai Ing-wen: President of the Republic of China from 2016 to 2024. Following the DPP's defeat in the 2008 presidential election, Tsai was elected party chair, a position she held three times (2008–2012, 2014–2018, and 2020–2022).
Born in Turin, this ruler of Sardinia became the first king of a united Italy in 1861 and earned a nickname echoing an ancient Roman imperial title, 'Father of the Fatherland.' Who was he?
Victor Emmanuel II: King of Italy from 1861 to 1878.

Fought alongside a wider Georgian civil conflict, this early-1990s fight pitted government forces against separatists backed by North Caucasian militants, Cossacks, and the Russian military — which conflict?
War in Abkhazia (1992–1993): Conflict between Georgia and Abkhaz separatists.
After an evangelical conversion in 1785, this Yorkshire MP spent two decades leading the parliamentary fight that ended Britain's slave trade — who was he?
William Wilberforce: English politician and abolitionist (1759–1833)
What is this — “Aniconic representation of the Hindu goddess Shakti, consort of Shiva”?

Yoni: Aniconic representation of the Hindu goddess Shakti, consort of Shiva. Yoni (Sanskrit: योनि, IAST: yoni), sometimes called pindika, is an abstract or aniconic representation of the Hindu goddess Shakti.
Which of these people was born first?
Ellen Swallow Richards (born 1842) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Zhuge Liang (born 181) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the oldest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
Marie Curie is a physicist. Curie was born in Warsaw, Russian Empire, where she studied at the clandestine Flying University and began her practical scientific training.
Which one below is best known as a chemist?
Mai Thi Nguyen-Kim is a chemist. Mai Thi Nguyen-Kim is a German chemist, science communicator, television presenter and YouTuber.
What is the atomic number of Unbiunium?
Unbiunium, also known as eka-actinium or element 121, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has symbol Ubu and atomic number 121.
In what year was Carl Linnaeus born?
Carl Linnaeus: Linnaeus was the son of a curate and was born in Råshult, in the countryside of Småland, southern Sweden.
In what year was Bernard Arnault born?
Bernard Arnault: Bernard Jean Étienne Arnault (born 5 March 1949) is a French businessman.
In what year was Jens Stoltenberg born?
Jens Stoltenberg was born in Oslo to diplomat and politician Thorvald Stoltenberg and politician Karin Stoltenberg (née Heiberg).
In what year did Jim Lovell die?
Jim Lovell: James Arthur Lovell Jr. (LUV-əl; March 25, 1928 – August 7, 2025) was an American astronaut, naval aviator, test pilot, and mechanical engineer.
In what year did Werner Heisenberg die?
Werner Heisenberg: Heisenberg published his Umdeutung paper in 1925, a major reinterpretation of old quantum theory.
In what year was Uranium discovered?
Uranium is a chemical element; it has symbol U and atomic number 92.
In what year was Cobalt discovered?
Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.
Ciprofloxacin: Pfizer. Ciprofloxacin, sold under the brand name Cipro among others, is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic used to treat a number of bacterial infections.
Which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-25 from?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-25: Soviet Union. Designed by the Soviet Union's Mikoyan-Gurevich bureau, it is an aircraft built primarily using stainless steel.
Who is credited with discovering Tucana?
Tucana: Petrus Plancius. Tucana (The Toucan) is a constellation in the southern sky, named after the toucan, a South American bird.
Who is credited with discovering Cro-Magnon?
Cro-Magnon: Louis Lartet. Cro-Magnons produced Upper Palaeolithic cultures, the first major one being the Aurignacian, which was succeeded by the Gravettian by 30,000 years ago.
Who is credited with discovering Makemake?
Makemake: Michael E. Brown. Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this family of hook-billed raptors includes buzzards, vultures, and kites across 75 genera — which family is this?
Accipitridae is one of the four families within the order Accipitriformes, and is a family of small to large birds of prey with strongly hooked bills and variable morphology based on diet.
This English academic and broadcaster, an anatomist and archaeologist by training, was president of the charity Humanists UK from 2019 to 2022 — who is she?
Alice Roberts (born 19 May 1973) is an English academic, anatomist, archaeologist, TV presenter and author.

Native to tropical America and carried across the Pacific by Spanish traders aboard the Manila galleons, this small tree in the same family as soursop produces a scaly-skinned fruit with sweet, creamy flesh — what's the species?
Annona squamosa is a small, well-branched tree or shrub from the family Annonaceae that bears edible fruits called sugar apples or sweetsops or custard apples.

Explicitly describing the relativity of motion and, by his own account, 23 years old in 499 CE, this figure is considered the first of the great mathematician-astronomers of classical Indian science — who is he?
Aryabhata (476-550 CE) was the first of the major mathematician-astronomers and early physicist from the classical age of Indian mathematics and Indian astronomy.

An Arctic and sub-Arctic cetacean, it is one of two living members of the family Monodontidae and is also known as the white whale (the only cetacean regularly occurring with this color) and the sea canary for its high-pitched calls. What is it?
Beluga whale (Delphinapterus leucas), is an Arctic and sub-Arctic cetacean.
Element 107, a synthetic transactinide whose most stable known isotope lasts barely 2.4 minutes, takes its name from a famous Danish physicist — what is it?
Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
This general-purpose, multi-paradigm programming language was designed at Microsoft by Anders Hejlsberg and first widely released in 2000, later becoming an international standard. What is it?
C Sharp (programming language) is a general-purpose high-level programming language supporting multiple paradigms.
Belonging to the trumpet-vine family Bignoniaceae, this tree genus thrives across warm parts of North America, the Caribbean, and East Asia — what is it called?
Catalpa is a genus of flowering plants in the family Bignoniaceae, native to warm temperate and subtropical regions of North America, the Caribbean, and East Asia.

A long-term lung condition that makes breathing progressively harder due to damaged airways and lung tissue, this condition develops gradually and currently cannot be cured, though treatments and lifestyle changes help manage symptoms. What is this disease, commonly abbreviated?
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a long-term lung condition that makes it progressively harder to breathe.
This bird's name comes from the Quechua word 'kuntur,' and its California-dwelling relative was nearly wiped out by habitat loss — which giant vulture soars over the Andes?
Condor is the common name for two genera of New World vultures, each with one extant species.
Present in the cytoplasm of bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotic cells alike, this dynamic protein-filament network stabilizes tissue and enables cells to migrate — what is it?
Cytoskeleton is a complex, dynamic network of interlinking protein filaments present in the cytoplasm of all cells, including those of bacteria and archaea.

Derived from the wild rock dove and split into more than 350 distinct breeds, this domesticated bird was already being bred by Mesopotamians more than 5,000 years ago, according to cuneiform tablets — what's the bird?
Domestic pigeon (Columba livia "domestica" or Columba livia forma domestica) is a domesticated bird derived from the rock dove (Columba livia), of which it is also a subspecies.
Born in Pretoria and emigrating to Canada in 1989, this CEO of Tesla and SpaceX co-founded a web software company called Zip2 back in 1995 — who is he?
Elon Musk (born June 28, 1971) is a businessman and former public official who is the CEO and largest shareholder of Tesla and SpaceX.
This American businessman co-founded a disappearing-photo messaging app and became the world's youngest billionaire in 2015 — who is he?
Evan Spiegel (born June 4, 1990) is an American businessman who is the co-founder and CEO of Snap Inc.
This Caltech chemical engineer won the 2018 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for using 'directed evolution' to engineer enzymes, and later joined Alphabet's board — who is she?
Frances Arnold (born July 25, 1956) is an American chemical engineer and Nobel Laureate.
The last living species in an order that first appeared over 290 million years ago, this disease-resistant "living fossil" with fan-shaped leaves is also called the maidenhair tree — which is it?
Ginkgo biloba (-goh), also known as the maidenhair tree, and often misspelled "gingko" (see Etymology below) is a species of gymnosperm tree native to East Asia.
What protein filament, grown from follicles in the skin's dermis layer and composed mainly of alpha-keratin, is one of the defining characteristics of mammals?
Hair is a protein filament that grows from follicles found in the dermis.

Known taxonomically as Lonicera, this genus of 158 species of arching shrubs and twining vines is native to northern latitudes worldwide, though one of its Asian members has become a notorious invasive pest — what's the plant?
Honeysuckle are arching shrubs or twining vines in the genus Lonicera of the family Caprifoliaceae.

A leading figure among Israel's 'New Historians,' this scholar characterizes the 1948 Palestinian expulsion as a deliberate campaign in his research and now teaches at the University of Exeter — who is he?
Ilan Pappé (born 7 November 1954) is an Israeli historian and political scientist, known for his work on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and as a leading figure among the New Historians.
Trained in biochemistry and physiology before ranging into geography and anthropology, this American author won the 1998 Pulitzer for Guns, Germs, and Steel — who is he?
Jared Diamond (born September 10, 1937) is an American scientist, historian, and author.
Born in 1972, this Canadian atmospheric scientist holds an endowed public-policy chair at Texas Tech and in 2021 became Chief Scientist at the Nature Conservancy — who is she?
Katharine Hayhoe (born 1972) is a Canadian atmospheric scientist.
Representing the Nemean Lion slain by Heracles as one of his twelve labors, this zodiac constellation sits between Cancer and Virgo — which constellation?
Leo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac, between Cancer, the Crab, to the west and Virgo, the Maiden, to the east.
This Berkeley professor upended classical logic by proposing 'fuzzy' mathematics — fuzzy sets, fuzzy logic, fuzzy control, and more — who was he?

Lotfi A. Zadeh (4 February 1921 - 6 September 2017) was a mathematician, computer scientist, electrical engineer, artificial intelligence researcher, and professor of computer science at the University of California, Berkeley.

This Milanese thinker was the first woman to write a mathematics handbook and the first appointed a mathematics professor — though she spent her final decades on theology and serving the poor. Who was she?
Maria Gaetana Agnesi (16 May 1718 - 9 January 1799) was a Milanese mathematician, philosopher, theologian, and humanitarian.
This hedge fund manager and licensed physician was among the first to predict and profit from the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis, later portrayed on screen in The Big Short. Who is he?
Michael Burry (born June 19, 1971) is an American investor, hedge fund manager, and licensed physician.
This Turkish government minister for environment and climate will preside over the 2026 UN Climate Change Conference, COP31 — who is he?
Murat Kurum is the minister of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change in Turkey, and president of the 2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference, COP31.

A former director of Russia's FSB intelligence agency, this politician served as Secretary of the Security Council of Russia from 2008 to 2024 and is considered one of Putin's closest advisors — who is he?
Nikolai Patrushev (born 11 July 1951) is a Russian politician, security officer and former intelligence officer who served as the secretary of the Security Council of Russia from 2008 to 2024.
Chemists still debate the exact definition, but generally, any large molecule containing a carbon-hydrogen or carbon-carbon bond falls into this broad class of compounds. What is it?
Organic compound are a subclass of chemical compounds of carbon.
This pulse crop, given the scientific name Pisum sativum by Linnaeus in 1753, is usually eaten as a vegetable via its small round seeds. What is it?
Pea is a pulse or fodder crop, but the word often refers to the seed or sometimes the pod of this flowering plant species.
Odorless when pure but reeking of rotting fish in technical grade, this colorless PH3 gas can burst into a luminous flame on contact with air — what highly toxic compound is it?
Phosphine (IUPAC name: phosphane) is a colorless, flammable, highly toxic compound with the chemical formula PH3, classed as a pnictogen hydride.

Attacks of this condition — abdominal pain, vomiting, and confusion lasting days to weeks — stem from a buildup of porphyrins and can be triggered by stress, smoking, or certain medications. What is it?
Porphyria (or) is a group of disorders in which substances called porphyrins build up in the body, adversely affecting the skin or nervous system.
Found in nucleic acids as the building block behind adenine and guanine, this nitrogen-rich heterocyclic compound is the most common of its kind in nature — what is it?
Purine is a heterocyclic aromatic organic compound that consists of two rings (pyrimidine and imidazole) fused together.

One of the rarest and most valuable precious metals, this hard, corrosion-resistant transition metal with only one naturally occurring isotope is prized for enhancing jewelry — what's the element (symbol Rh, atomic number 45)?
Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
Having taught economics at the Catholic University of Asunción and once served as Paraguay's finance minister, this politician assumed his country's presidency in 2023 — who is he?
Santiago Peña (Spanish; born 16 November 1978) is a Paraguayan politician and economist who has served as the 52nd president of Paraguay since 2023.

Dubbed the "father of modern differential geometry," this Chinese-born American mathematician and poet won the Wolf Prize — and has a medal named for him by the International Mathematical Union. Who was he?
Shiing-Shen Chern (pinyin: Chn Xngshn; October 26, 1911 - December 3, 2004) was a Chinese-born American mathematician and poet.

Meaning 'pore bearer' in Greek, this phylum of sessile, filter-feeding marine invertebrates has tube-like bodies of jelly-like material sandwiched between thin cell layers, letting water circulate through countless pores — name the animal group?
Sponge are primarily marine invertebrates of the animal phylum Porifera (meaning 'pore bearer').
This South African biologist established the tiny roundworm C. elegans as a model organism, work that helped earn him a share of the 2002 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Who was he?
Sydney Brenner (13 January 1927 - 5 April 2019) was a South African biologist.
Raised in Michigan with little schooling, he sold his first inventions by age 22 and moved to New York to chase engineering — going on to become one of America's most famous inventors. Who?
Thomas Edison (February 11, 1847 - October 18, 1931) was an American inventor and businessman.
Caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis and treated with the antibiotic streptomycin, this tick-borne illness also goes by an animal-related nickname — what is it?
Tularemia is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis.
This Russian-American inventor built a television system using cathode-ray tubes and worked on image tubes and the electron microscope — who was he?
Vladimir K. Zworykin (1888/1889 - July 29, 1982) was a Russian-American inventor, engineer, and pioneer of television technology.
The first woman ever to serve as Ukraine's prime minister, this politician held that post in 2005 and again from 2007 to 2010, and now leads the Batkivshchyna political party — who is she?

Yulia Tymoshenko (ne Hrihyan; born 27 November 1960) is a Ukrainian politician, who served as Prime Minister of Ukraine in 2005, and again from 2007 until 2010; the first woman in Ukraine to hold that position.
Nicknamed the 'upside-down tree' for its unusual silhouette, this genus of long-lived African and Malagasy giants was named after a French naturalist — what genus is it?
Adansonia: Genus of trees known as baobab.
Made in the adrenal cortex, this hormone tells the kidney to hang onto sodium and dump potassium, quietly steering your blood pressure and blood volume — what is it?
A colourless gas of nitrogen and hydrogen with a famously pungent smell, this compound has about 70% of its industrial output turned into fertilisers — what is it?
Ammonia: Chemical compound. A stable binary hydride and the simplest pnictogen hydride, ammonia is a colourless gas with a distinctive pungent smell.
Born Fernando Martins de Bulhões, this 13th-century Portuguese Catholic priest joined the Order of Friars Minor — who is he?
Anthony of Padua: Portuguese Catholic saint (1195–1231)
Known as common wormwood, this bitter herb native to North Africa and temperate Eurasia lends its name and flavor to a notorious green spirit — which plant?
Artemisia absinthium: Species of plant. It is grown as an ornamental plant and is used as an ingredient in the spirit absinthe and some other alcoholic beverages.
Whose name derives from the Sanskrit word 'nimba,' this Mahogany-family tree native to South Asia is the source of a widely used pesticidal oil — which species, and not one of these animals?
Azadirachta indica: Species of plant. Azadirachta indica, commonly known as neem, margosa, nimtree or Indian lilac, is a tree in the Mahogany family Meliaceae.
Sold under the brand name Tessalon, this cough-relief medication works within about 20 minutes by acting as a local anesthetic that blocks stretch receptors in the lungs — what is this drug called?
Benzonatate: Oral cough medication. Benzonatate, sold under the brand name Tessalon among others, is a medication that is used for the symptomatic relief of cough.
Despite being just 12 to 20 cm long, this small marine creature's vivid markings flash brighter when it feels threatened, and its bite delivers a neurotoxin called tetrodotoxin — what is it?
Blue-ringed octopus: Four species of mollusk.

This tropical tree's moderately ripe flesh, once cooked, is said to taste like a fresh-baked loaf with a potato-like flavor, and 18th-century navigators carried it in seedless form to the Caribbean — what is it?
Breadfruit: Edible fruit-bearing tree in family. Moraceae.
This intensely sour citrus hybrid — a cross between a kumquat and likely a mandarin orange — is a staple of Philippine cooking and also popular in Malaysian and Indonesian cuisine — which fruit?
Calamansi: Hybrid species of citrus. Calamansi (Citrus × microcarpa), also known as calamondin, Philippine lime, or Philippine lemon, is a citrus hybrid cultivated predominantly in the Philippines.
Extracted from the cochineal insect, this bright-red pigment is also known by the food-additive code E120 — what is it called?
Carmine: Pigment, aluminium salt of carminic acid.
The biochemist hailed as the "father" of industrial fermentation, instrumental in the 1917 Balfour Declaration, became the first president of Israel — who was he?
Chaim Weizmann: Israeli statesman and British chemist (1874–1952)
Native to the Andean forests of South America, this genus of trees is nicknamed the 'fever tree' because its bark yields quinine, the only effective malaria treatment for centuries — what is it?
Cinchona: Genus of plants, source of quinine.
Used to treat gout, familial Mediterranean fever, and pericarditis, this medication has such a narrow therapeutic index that its injectable form was pulled from the US market in 2008. What is it?
Colchicine: Medication mainly used to treat gout. The American College of Rheumatology recommends colchicine, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or steroids in the treatment of gout.

Describing how closely two variables move together, this statistical measure is famously not proof of causation, and two variables can even be linked this way without truly depending on each other — what is it called?
Correlation: Statistical relationship. In statistics, correlation is a type of statistical relationship between two random variables or bivariate data.
Making up about 80 percent water and mostly colorless, this catch-all term covers everything inside a cell's outer membrane except its nucleus — what is it?
Cytoplasm: All of the contents of a cell including organelles but excluding the nucleus.

Marked by deep gasping breaths and breath that smells oddly fruity or like acetone, this life-threatening condition arises when a shortage of insulin forces the body to burn fat into acidic ketones — what is it?
Diabetic ketoacidosis: Medical condition. Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a potentially life-threatening acute complication of diabetes mellitus.
The tallest of the three camel species, standing up to 2.4 meters at the shoulder, which animal carries a single hump of fat on its back?
First described in 1821, this family of large herbivorous mammals features a snout modified into a trunk and includes extinct relatives such as mammoths — which taxonomic family?
Elephantidae: Family of mammals. The family was first described by John Edward Gray in 1821, and later assigned to taxonomic ranks within the order Proboscidea.

Arising in the food pipe that runs between the throat and the stomach, this disease's two main subtypes are a squamous-cell form common in the developing world and a glandular form more common in developed nations. What is it?
Esophageal cancer: Malignant neoplastic disease of the esophagus.
While its deciduous neighbors drop everything and go bare for winter, this kind of plant keeps its foliage green and working all year round — what's the botanical term?
Evergreen: Plant that has leaves in all seasons.
This beetle family produces light mainly at twilight to attract mates — though some females mimic another species' flash pattern just to lure and eat the males — what are they commonly called?
Firefly: Family of beetles. The Lampyridae are a family of elateroid beetles with more than 2,400 described species, many of which are light-emitting.
A French economist who gave up accounting to lecture across France, he founded peace societies and the Inter-Parliamentary Union before sharing the very first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901. Who was he?
Frédéric Passy: French economist and pacifist (1822–1912)

Among the longest of all living crocodilians, this fish-eater wields a slender snout lined with 110 interlocking teeth, and the males sport a bulbous, pot-shaped bump on the tip that gives the animal its name. What is it?
Gharial: Crocodilian native to the Indian subcontinent.
This branch of discrete mathematics studies structures made of vertices connected by edges, modeling pairwise relationships between objects — what field is it?

Graph theory: Area of discrete mathematics. In mathematics and computer science, graph theory is the study of graphs, which are mathematical structures used to model pairwise relations between objects.

This prehensile, multi-fingered body part sits at the end of primates' forelimbs — koalas famously have two opposable thumbs on each one, while raccoons are often said to have them despite lacking true opposable thumbs. What is it?
Hand: Extremity at the end of an arm or forelimb.
Also known as the cane spider or giant crab spider, this huntsman species native to the tropics has spread to subtropical regions worldwide — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria: Species of spider. It is native to the tropical regions of the world, and it is present in some subtropical areas as an introduced species.
Marketed as Hydrodiuril, this medication treats high blood pressure and fluid retention by blocking sodium and chloride reabsorption in the kidneys' distal tubules — what drug is it?

Hydrochlorothiazide: Diuretic medication. Hydrochlorothiazide, sold under the brand name Hydrodiuril among others, is a diuretic medication used to treat hypertension and swelling due to fluid build-up.
Making up roughly 75% of antibodies found in the human bloodstream, which antibody type is produced by plasma B cells and features two paratopes?
A Harvard chemistry professor who studied chlorophyll and helped develop poison gas in WWI, he later became Harvard's president and the first U.S. ambassador to West Germany — who is he?
This New Zealand-American sexologist at Johns Hopkins coined the very phrases 'gender role' and 'sexual orientation' — which controversial researcher is it?
John Money: New Zealand psychologist and sexologist (1921–2006)

With oversized heads, dagger-like bills, and stubby tails, these 118 brightly colored bird species swoop from perches to nab prey — and despite reputation, many don't even live near water — what family of birds?
Kingfisher: Family of birds. The family contains 118 species and is divided into three subfamilies and 19 genera.
He fathered the Ford Mustang in the 1960s, then rescued Chrysler from collapse as its CEO in the 1980s — one of the rare executives to run two of Detroit's Big Three. Who?
Nicknamed for the Greek goddess of wisdom, this roughly 22-centimeter nocturnal bird was introduced to Britain in the late 1800s and to New Zealand's South Island soon after — which species?
Little owl: Species of owl. It was introduced into Britain at the end of the 19th century and into the South Island of New Zealand in the early 20th century.
Nicknamed the 'maker of modern Mysore,' this Indian civil engineer and statesman's birthday is now celebrated as Engineer's Day across India, Sri Lanka, and Tanzania — who is he?
M. Visvesvaraya: Indian civil engineer, administrator, and former prime minister of Mysore Kingdom.

Studying under Rutherford at the Cavendish Lab, this Adelaide-born physicist discovered the nuclei of helium-3 and tritium and helped achieve the first experimental nuclear fusion — who was this Australian humanitarian?
Also nicknamed 'Cornish salmon,' this predatory fish is often netted alongside the Atlantic herring it preys on, and is heavily overfished across European waters — which fish?
Merluccius merluccius: Species of fish. Merluccius merluccius or the European hake is a merluccid hake of the genus Merluccius.
Known to NATO as 'Halo,' this Soviet-designed aircraft holds the record as the largest helicopter ever built in serial production — which one?
Mil Mi-26: Soviet/Russian heavy transport helicopter.
Numbering roughly 160,000 species and mostly active at night, these insects share an order with butterflies but are known for their duller, darker wings — what are they?
Moth: Group of mostly-nocturnal insects in the order Lepidoptera.
Also called the belly button, this flat or hollowed spot on the abdomen marks where the umbilical cord once attached — what is it?
Navel: Scarred area on the abdomen after detachment of the umbilical cord.
Nicknamed the 'winter vomiting disease' and spread by the fecal-oral route, this is the most common cause of gastroenteritis — what is it?
Norovirus: Type of viruses that cause gastroenteritis.

Numbering 126 species, these are the largest order of marsupials in the Western Hemisphere — and only one of them, the Virginia variety, made it as far north as the United States and Canada. What animal is this?
Nicknamed the 'white rats' of its phylum for how often it's cultivated in classrooms and labs, this single-celled ciliate thrives in stagnant ponds — what is it?
Known for its speed, this large crow-sized raptor has a blue-grey back, barred white underparts, and a black head — an avivore with marked sexual dimorphism — what is it?
Peregrine falcon: Fastest known animal and common bird of prey.
This branch of biology studies how organs, cells, and biomolecules carry out their functions, and gives its name, alongside medicine, to a Nobel Prize category — which field?
Physiology: Science regarding functions in organisms or living systems.
First domesticated some 5,000 years ago on the Iranian plateau, this fruit-bearing shrub reached California in 1769 via Spanish settlers — which fruit?
Pomegranate: Fruit-bearing deciduous shrub. Pomegranate was first domesticated by ancient Iranians in the Iranian plateau and nearby regions about 5,000 years ago.
This thorny European shrub's tart fruit gives sloe gin its name in Britain, while its wood becomes the classic Irish walking stick — what is it?
Prunus spinosa: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
Domesticated in Asia, this crunchy root vegetable in the mustard family owes its peppery bite to compounds like glucosinolate — what vegetable is it?
Radish: Root vegetable of the Brassicaceae family. The radish (Raphanus sativus or Raphanus raphanistrum subsp. sativus) is a flowering plant in the mustard family, Brassicaceae.
Named from Greek words for 'rose' and 'tree,' this flowering shrub genus is Nepal's national flower and includes azaleas as a subgenus — which plant?
Rhododendron: Genus of flowering plants. Azaleas make up two subgenera of Rhododendron.
This Japanese botanist lived and worked during the Meiji era of the late 19th century — who was he?
Ryōkichi Yatabe: Japanese botanist and poet. Ryōkichi Yatabe (矢田部良吉; October 13, 1851 – August 8, 1899) was a Japanese botanist during the Meiji era.
Sitting near the center of the Milky Way between Libra and Sagittarius, this zodiac constellation's recognition predates ancient Greek culture — which constellation?
